title: Snake game logic with a text board
prompt:
Build the logic of a Snake game in Python as a package snake/ with snake/__init__.py, snake/game.py and snake/board.py (no graphics library).
- snake/game.py: class Game(width, height, seed=0). Coordinates are (x, y) with (0, 0) at the top left. The snake starts as one cell at (width // 2, height // 2) moving "right"; game.snake is a list of cells with the head first; game.score starts at 0; game.over starts False. Food: game.food is a cell, placed with random.Random(seed) choosing from the free cells in sorted order (tests may also set game.food directly).
  step(direction=None) moves one cell. direction is "up", "down", "left" or "right"; None keeps the current one; turning straight back (e.g. "left" while moving "right") is ignored when the snake is longer than 1. Moving onto the food grows the snake by one (the tail stays), adds 1 to score and places new food. Hitting a wall or the snake's own body sets over = True and the snake does not move. step returns True while the game goes on and False once it is over (also for every later call, which changes nothing).
- snake/board.py: render(game) -> a string of height lines of width characters: '.' empty, '@' head, 'o' body, '*' food, joined by "\n".
snake/__init__.py exposes Game and render. Write unit tests too.
